title: Lumbini, traditional birthplace of the Buddha
summary: Pilgrimage site in the Nepalese Terai that Buddhist tradition names as the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama. An Ashokan pillar inscription of the 3rd century BCE marks it, and excavations beneath the Maya Devi Temple found a timber structure dated to the 6th century BCE under later brick shrines.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 6th-century-BCE timber structure found under the Maya Devi Temple (EurekAlert report of the Antiquity study); the range is a century either side. The Buddha's traditional birth year, given by UNESCO as 623 BCE, is tradition and is debated by scholars. End is the present: the site is still a pilgrimage place.
